description: We are building Outpost Commander, a free browser game for students aged 10-15. Players run a Moon or Mars outpost and share limited power between oxygen, water, food, heat and science, using NASA life-support data. Made by an IT teacher from Jizzakh, Uzbekistan, in English and Uzbek.
summary: Outpost Commander is a free browser game for students aged 10–15. Players command a Moon or Mars outpost with a crew of four for 12 days. Each day they divide limited power between an oxygen maker, a water recycler, a greenhouse, heaters and radiation shielding, and a science lab. The crew's daily needs come from NASA life-support data, so every decision has a real cost. The Moon mission teaches planning for the two-week lunar night; the Mars mission teaches resilience during dust storms and shows how MOXIE makes oxygen from Martian air. The game runs on any phone or computer, needs no installation, and works in English and Uzbek, so teachers like me can use it in real classrooms.
details: WHAT IT DOES: The player chooses the Moon or Mars and plans 12 days for a crew of four. Every day there is a limited number of power units (solar + battery, plus a small fission reactor on Mars). The player assigns units to five systems: oxygen maker (+1.7 kg O2; on the Moon it splits water and uses 1.9 kg of water), water recycler (+3.2 kg), greenhouse (+0.6 kg food, +0.15 kg O2), heaters and radiation shield (needed at night and in the cold) and science lab (+10 points). A live preview shows the result of each choice before the day ends. Unused power charges the battery. If oxygen, water or food runs out, or the crew gets cold, crew health drops. Goal: survive 12 days and reach 120 science points (up to 3 stars). EVENTS: micrometeoroid leak, solar flare (crew hides in the radiation shelter and science stops), lunar sunset, recycler clog, a 3-day Mars dust storm (-70% solar power), a harvest and an ice discovery. Every day shows a short NASA fact with a link to its source. The end screen explains four lessons: trade-offs, planning ahead, recycling and in-situ resource use. BENEFITS AND IMPACT: Students feel real numbers (a crew of four needs about 3.4 kg of oxygen per day) and real engineering trade-offs instead of memorising facts. Teachers get a free, bilingual (English and Uzbek) tool for a 15-20 minute lesson that works on phones. I plan to pilot it with first-year IT students at Jizzakh City Technical College No. 1, Uzbekistan. CREATIVITY: Two missions teach two different lessons: the Moon teaches planning (store energy before the two-week night; oxygen costs water), Mars teaches resilience (dust storms, reactor backup, MOXIE makes oxygen from the air). Both were balanced by simulation so a good plan wins and a greedy plan fails. TOOLS: HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single file, no frameworks and no installation; hosted on GitHub Pages; tested in Chromium on desktop and phone sizes. Source code: https://github.com/Begzod6880/outpost-commander
